LESSON: RHYTHM COMPOSING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: CREATING/
Topic 2.1: Rhythm COMPOSING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Rhythm COMPOSING. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Identify and mimic animals, objects that make rhythmic patterns for rhythm patterns using common names such awareness, as tea, coffee, soda, Coca-Cola, fish
2. improvise rhythmic accompaniment to short, simple, familiar songs to enhance compositional skills and for enjoyment,
3. create simple rhythmic patterns with short and long sounds and silences using body percussion for enjoyment,
4. create rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs as a basis for composition and for enjoyment 332 Property of the Government of Kenya e) on digital devices to make improvements after listening and for digital literacy.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Identify and mimic animals, objects that make rhythmic patterns for rhythm patterns using common names such awareness, as tea, coffee, soda, Coca-Cola, fish
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify and mimic animals, objects that make rhythmic patterns for rhythm patterns using common names such awareness, as tea, coffee, soda, Coca-Cola, fish. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. improvise rhythmic accompaniment to short, simple, familiar songs to enhance compositional skills and for enjoyment,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to improvise rhythmic accompaniment to short, simple, familiar songs to enhance compositional skills and for enjoyment,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. create simple rhythmic patterns with short and long sounds and silences using body percussion for enjoyment,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to create simple rhythmic patterns with short and long sounds and silences using body percussion for enjoyment,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. create rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs as a basis for composition and for enjoyment 332 Property of the Government of Kenya e) on digital devices to make improvements after listening and for digital literacy.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to create rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs as a basis for composition and for enjoyment 332 Property of the Government of Kenya e) on digital devices to make improvements after listening and for digital literacy. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Rhythm COMPOSING.
2. Explain Rhythm COMPOSING to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Rhythm COMPOSING.
4. Show that you can: Identify and mimic animals, objects that make rhythmic patterns for rhythm patterns using common names such awareness, as tea, coffee, soda, Coca-Cola, fish
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Rhythm COMPOSING. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Rhythm COMPOSING important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Identify and mimic animals, objects that make rhythmic patterns for rhythm patterns using common names such awareness, as tea, coffee, soda, Coca-Cola, fish
2. improvise rhythmic accompaniment to short, simple, familiar songs to enhance compositional skills and for enjoyment,
3. create simple rhythmic patterns with short and long sounds and silences using body percussion for enjoyment,
4. create rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs as a basis for composition and for enjoyment 332 Property of the Government of Kenya e) on digital devices to make improvements after listening and for digital literacy.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
